label: Person
name: Albano Bortoletto Cavallin
summary:
Albano Bortoletto Cavallin (b. 1941) is a Brazilian Catholic bishop who has served in various dioceses in Brazil, representing the Italian immigrant Catholic tradition of northern Brazil's agricultural frontier regions. Born in Rio Grande do Sul to an Italian immigrant family, he was ordained a priest and subsequently consecrated bishop to serve in dioceses of the Brazilian interior.

His ministry exemplifies a common pattern in twentieth-century Brazilian Catholicism: priests from the strongly Catholic Italian immigrant communities of the southern states were often sent as missionaries and bishops to the ecclesiastically underdeveloped frontier regions of the north and centre-west. This movement of southern Brazilian clergy to the frontier carried the vigorous parish culture of the Italian immigrant community into new territories.

Bortoletto Cavallin's episcopate engaged the pastoral challenges typical of frontier Brazilian Catholicism: scattered rural communities, land conflict, indigenous peoples' rights, and the social upheavals of agricultural colonisation. His Italian-Brazilian background provided him with a tradition of strong popular Catholic practice that he could nurture and develop in his adopted diocese.
